source_text:
Τοίνυν κολληθῶμεν τοῖς μετ’ εὐσεβείας εἰρηνεύουσιν, καὶ μὴ τοῖς μεθ̓ ὑποκρίσεως βουλομένοις εἰρήνην.
λέγει γάρ που: Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἄπεστιν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ.
καὶ πάλιν: Τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν εὐλογοῦσιν, τῇ δὲ καρδίᾳ αὐτῶν κατηρῶντο.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἠγάπησαν αὐτὸν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν καὶ τῇ γλώσσῃ αὐτῶν ἐψεύσαντο αὐτόν, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν οὐκ εὐθεῖα μετ’ αὐτοῦ, οὐδὲ ἐπιστώθησαν ἐν τῇ διαθήκῃ αὐτοῦ.
διὰ τοῦτο ἄλαλα γενηθήτω τὰ χείηλ τὰ δόλια τὰ λαλοῦντα κατὰ τοῦ δικαίου ἀνομίαν. καὶ πάλιν: Ἐξολεθρεύσαι κύριος πάντα τὰ χείλη τὰ δόλια, γλῶσσαν μεγαλορήμονα, τοὺς εἰπόντας: Τὴν γλῶσσαν ἡμῶν μεγαλυνοῦμεν, τὰ χείλη ἡμῶν παῤ ἡμῖν ἐστιν: τίς ἡμῶν κύριός ἐστιν;
ἀπὸ τῆς ταλαιπωρίας τῶν πτωχῶν καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ τῶν πενήτων νῦν ἀναστήσομαι, λέγει κύριος: θήσομαι ἐν σωτηρίῳ,
παρρησιάσομαι ἐν αὐτῷ.
thought_title: Cling to the Sincere Peacemakers, Not the Hypocrites
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, is urging the Corinthians to separate themselves from the faction and to join those who pursue peace sincerely, supporting this with scriptural quotations about hypocritical lips and hearts.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore let us cling to those who with piety make peace, and not to those who with hypocrisy wish peace. For he says somewhere: This people with their lips honors me, but their heart is far distant from me. And again: With their mouth they bless, but with their heart they cursed. And again he says: They loved him with their mouth and with their tongue they lied to him, but their heart was not straight with him, nor were they faithful in his covenant. Because of this let the deceitful lips become speechless, the ones speaking lawlessness against the righteous. And again: May the Lord destroy all the deceitful lips, the boastful tongue, those who said: Our tongue we will magnify, our lips are with us; who is lord over us? From the misery of the poor and from the groaning of the needy now I will arise, says the Lord; I will place [him] in safety, I will speak boldly in him.

choices.why: The verb means to glue or join oneself closely; 'cling' preserves the physical intimacy of the metaphor and the hortatory subjunctive force.

choices.english: those who with piety make peace
choices.why: The participle with the prepositional phrase is kept as a single unit; 'make peace' renders the active verb, and 'with piety' preserves the adverbial force of the prepositional phrase.

choices.english: those who with hypocrisy wish peace
choices.why: The contrast with the previous clause is sharpened by keeping the parallel structure; 'wish' renders βουλομένοις as a volitional participle, distinct from actually making peace.
rejected: those wishing for peace with hypocrisy

choices.why: The double expression of distance (πόρρω + ἄπεστιν) is preserved to reflect the emphatic separation in the source.
The passive imperative of γίνομαι with the predicate adjective is rendered literally; 'speechless' captures the loss of speech implied by ἄλαλα.
The middle voice of τίθημι with the prepositional phrase is rendered with an implied object; 'safety' renders σωτήριον as a concrete state of deliverance.
rejected: I will set him in salvation
I will appoint him to safety

pass_b_english: So let us cling to those who make peace with piety, and not to those who only wish for peace with hypocrisy.
For he says somewhere: “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far distant from me” (Isaiah 29:13).
And again: “With their mouth they blessed, but with their heart they cursed” (Psalm 62:4).
And again he says: “They loved him with their mouth and lied to him with their tongue, but their heart was not upright with him, nor were they faithful in his covenant” (Psalm 78:36 LXX).

For this reason let the deceitful lips that speak lawlessness against the righteous become speechless. And again: “May the Lord destroy all the deceitful lips, the boastful tongue, those who said: ‘We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; who is lord over us?’” (Psalm 12:3-4).
“Because of the misery of the poor and the groaning of the needy, now I will arise,” says the Lord; “I will place him in safety; I will speak boldly in him” (Psalm 12:5).
notes: χείηλ in the source is a misspelling of χείλη (lips); the gloss renders it as 'lips'.

last_rejected.ruling: The English labels the citation 'LXX', and Psalm 77:36-37 is the correct LXX numbering for 'Ἠγάπησαν αὐτὸν τῷ στόματι'. The label is not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: For this reason let the deceitful lips that speak lawlessness against the righteous become speechless.

last_rejected.why: This is a psalm quotation, but English gives it as Clement’s own command before “And again.”
last_rejected.fix: Quote it as Scripture: “For this reason let the deceitful lips that speak lawlessness against the righteous become speechless” (Psalm 31:18).
last_rejected.ruling: 'ἄλαλα γενηθήτω τὰ χείλη τὰ δόλια' is rendered accurately as an imperative. The source has no introductory formula, so the missing quote marks and citation change no meaning.
